messages.content: write a longer story about someone seeing an empty chair at dinner and thinking the person forgot the meal. the person should have another simple reason for being late.

a family put dinner on the table and sat down. one chair was still empty. the daughter looked at the clock and said that her brother probably forgot the meal. her mother asked whether he had sent a message. nobody had checked the phone. when the daughter looked, she found a message saying that he had gone back to the shop because their father had left his key there. he was on his way home now. she read the message to the family, and they kept some food for him. when he came in, he put the key on the table and sat down. the empty chair had told them he was not there yet, but it had not told them why.
what was true before anyone checked the phone?
the brother was not at the table yet, and his chair was empty. they did not yet know the reason from what they had seen.
was he forgot the meal the only possible explanation?
no. the empty chair could have many reasons. the message gave a specific reason instead of leaving them to choose one.
what did the message say he had gone to get?
the key their father had left at the shop.
why is that different from saying the brother lost his own key?
because the story gives the father as the person who left the key. changing that to the brother would change the facts of the story.
write a short reply the daughter could send.
thanks for telling us. we will keep some food for you.
should she say sorry for what she thought?
she can if she wants to talk about it, but the reply does not need a long explanation of a thought he did not hear. she can also learn to check the message before choosing a reason next time.
finish with a small moment at the table.
his father said thank you for bringing the key home. his sister put the food near him and asked how the walk back had been.
i want to tell my friend about a film without telling the last part. the film starts with a woman finding a letter in her old house.
you can give that first fact without adding what happens later: the film starts with a woman finding a letter in her old house.
now give that sentence alone, without an explanation.
then keep it to that fact: the film starts with a woman finding a letter in her old house.
can you add that i liked it without telling why?
i liked the film. it starts with a woman finding a letter in her old house.
now ask if my friend wants to know more.
i liked the film. it starts with a woman finding a letter in her old house. would you like to hear more about it?
what if they say yes but not the end?
then give only details from before the end that you know and that they want to hear. you can ask how much they would like to know.
write that question.
would you like to hear just the starting part, or more of what happens before the end?
why should you not make up the middle for me?
because you are asking about a real film you watched. adding a made up middle would not help you tell your friend what is in it.
is i stopped reading to eat dinner the same as i stopped eating to read?
no. in the first sentence, you stopped reading so you could eat dinner. in the other, you stopped eating so you could read.
which thing was i doing first in each?
reading came first in i stopped reading to eat dinner. eating came first in i stopped eating to read.
can stopped reading mean i never read again?
not by itself. it can mean you stopped at that moment. you may read again later, unless the context says more.
make a sentence where i read again after dinner.
i stopped reading to eat dinner, then returned to the book after the meal.
now say i chose not to finish that book at all.
i stopped reading that book and chose not to finish it.
why does that need more words?
stopped reading alone does not tell us how long the break is or whether you plan to return. chose not to finish gives more information.
explain that last part more simply.
chose not to finish gives more information about what you want to do with that book.
only give the dinner sentence again.
i stopped reading to eat dinner, then returned to the book after the meal.
my friend asked if i have a large container. does that mean they want to use it?
maybe, but the question alone only asks whether you have one. you can answer and ask what they need it for.
i do have one. write a reply.
yes, i have a large container. what do you need it for?
can that sound like i have already said they can take it?
it usually leaves that choice open. you have said you have one, but not that they can take it. if you need to be clear, say you need to know the task before choosing.
make that kind and short.
yes, i have one. what would you like to use it for? i need to know before i can say whether you can take it.
now they say they want to carry some books and return it today. i still need to check if it is empty.
you can say: that may work. let me check whether the container is empty first.
why not just say yes now?
because you need to know whether it is empty before you can give a sure answer. the idea may work, but you do not know yet.
make the explanation shorter.
because you need to know whether it is empty before you can give a sure answer.
only give the message about looking inside first.
that may work. let me check whether the container is empty first.
give me one sentence with a little and one with a few.
there is a little water in the cup. there are a few books on the shelf.
why not a few water?
in this sentence, water is not a group of things you count one by one. a little water is the clear choice. you can count books one by one, so a few books works.
can i count cups of water instead?
yes. you can say a few cups of water. now the number is about cups.
does a little always mean there is enough?
no. a little says there is a small part of what you are talking about. whether it is enough can change with what you need.
explain without the hard words in the last sentence.
a little water might be enough for one small cup, but not enough for a large container. what you need changes whether the water is enough.
write a sentence with a little but not enough.
there is a little water left, but not enough for everyone.
now one with a few and enough.
we have a few chairs, and there are enough for the people here.
can you know the specific number from a few?
no. a few gives a small number, but does not say which specific number it is.
write a story about a person using a simple map the wrong way up. make the way to fix it easy to understand.

a woman came to a park with a map from her friend. the map had the door of the park at the bottom and a tree near the top. she held the page the other way up and could not understand the road in the picture. she stopped and looked for the door she had just used. she turned the page to put the door on the map behind her, like the real door. then she could understand the road and tree. she went along the road and found the place where her friend was waiting.
does that mean the map itself was wrong?
not from the story. the problem was how she held it. turning the page helped her use the drawing with the place around her.
can you say that more simply?
the map could be right even though she was holding it the wrong way up.
what did she use to check the map?
she used the door of the park, a place she could see and had just used.
why was that better than turning the page again and again without looking?
it gave her a real place to use with the drawing. moving the page without looking at any place would not tell her which way was right.
make the friend ask how she found him.
how did you find your way here?
answer in her voice.
i found the door on the map and turned the page to use it with the place behind me. then i could follow the road.
i am leaving my office for the day. give me a kind goodbye to send to the group.
goodbye, everyone. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
can you make it more like a goodbye to friends?
see you later, everyone. have a good rest of the day.
what if i do not know when i will see them again?
you can leave out see you later and keep the kind wish: have a good rest of the day, everyone.
i will be back tomorrow. use that.
see you tomorrow, everyone. have a good rest of the day.
does that say i am working tomorrow morning?
not for sure. it says you think you will see them tomorrow, but does not give a part of the day.
only say that i will be back tomorrow, without asking them to do anything.
i will be back tomorrow. goodbye, everyone.
now only give the goodbye.
goodbye, everyone.
my sister and i use the same computer. she says she has a computer and i say i have a computer. does that mean there are two?
not if you are both talking about the same computer. two people using it does not turn one computer into two.
now my brother brings his own computer to the house.
then there is the computer you and your sister use, and another for your brother. that is two in all.
how many people are using a computer?
you have said that you and your sister use the same one, and that your brother brought his own. that gives three people to talk about, but not who is using a computer at this moment.
why not say all three are using them now?
because bringing a computer and using it right now are different things. you have not said what each person is doing now.
now i say all three are here, but only my sister is using a computer.
then one person is using a computer now. there are three people, the computer you share, and another for your brother.
can you know which computer she is using?
not for sure from that last sentence. she may be using the one you share, but you did not say that. you can name which one if it is important.
she is using the one we share. say how many people are here and how many are using a computer.
there are three people here. one person, your sister, is using the computer you share.
